judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard party-identification recital; the only oddity is the run-together typography ('THISFARMOUTAGREEMENTDATED') and the open-ended phrase 'shall be effective as hereinafter provided', which leaves the effective date to be found elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 17 says the Agreement is effective 'as of the date first above written', which supplies the missing referent, so the deferral is resolved rather than contradicted; the undated Exhibits A, C and D are blanks in forms rather than an operative conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite payment term ($2,000 concurrent with execution) with no ambiguous word to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in a WHEREAS recital rather than the operative sections, and the operative location-fee obligation in 3(B)(2) covers only Subsequent Wells, so the initial fee lives only in a recital — a modest recital-vs-operative tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reservation of 'all rights associated with' the 2000' circle around Well KF-1053 is broad, and the tract numbers are OCR-mangled, but the carve-out itself is geometrically definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the parallel carve-outs in Section 2(D) and the Exhibit 'A' footnote ('less and except those portions ... lying in a 2,000' radius circle'), though 2(D) says 'centered around' where the recital says 'surrounding'; a recital granting that 'Farmee may acquire an interest' also sits loosely against the operative earning mechanics of 3(D).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure incorporation list; the only wrinkle is that Exhibit 'C' is called a 'Geological Requirement Letter' while the attached Exhibit C is headed 'Geological Requirements' and is not a letter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B-1 is referenced here and in Section 16 but the attached plat material is largely illegible, and Exhibit C is expressly relied on by Sections 3(D) and 10(A); the mismatch of labels is trivial and no operative conflict appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Completed well' is defined to include a plugged and abandoned dry hole, an unusual definition that could be read against the ordinary meaning of 'completed'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The operative text almost never uses the defined 'completed well', speaking instead of a well 'completed as a well capable of production in paying quantities' (3(D)) and of 'drills and completes' (Section 16), so the definition and usage do not line up cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definition keyed to regulatory field rules with an 'e.g.' list; the illustration is open-ended but the referent is externally fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in 3(A)(1) and 3(B)(1) for well locations on units including Farmout Lands; nothing else in the instrument redefines it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular in form — an 'earning well' is one by which Farmee is entitled to an assignment — but the entitlement conditions are stated in 3(D).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term 'earning well' appears nowhere in the operative text (3(F) speaks of 'earning requirements'), so it is a dangling definition rather than a conflicting one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The acreage circles are precise, but 'capable of producing in paying quantities' is the classic oil-and-gas phrase courts construe, and the emphatic 'that portion and only that portion' invites argument about rights outside the circle.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 3(E) (depths earned) and 3(D)(1) (which defines Operating Rights Earned by cross-reference to this subsection) and with Exhibit D's blank 'acre circle'; the interaction between the 80/40-acre circles and the drilling-unit locations permitted by 3(A)(1) is not fully worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'and other similar burdens on production' is a general catch-all appended to an enumerated list, the classic ejusdem generis setup.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined term 'lease burdens' is never used in the operative text (Section 15(A) speaks of 'obligations, burdens and requirements'), so the catch-all has little to bite on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise depth definition with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used only in 3(C) (substitute wells), and 3(E) independently caps earned depths at 4,000', so the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; 'the initial well' is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3(A) which names the first well the 'test well' and with 2(I) which defines subsequent wells by reference to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition requires the well to have 'previously produced' and to be capable of producing in 'commercial quantities', a standard that differs from the 'paying quantities' formula used everywhere else in the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7(A) imposes shut-in royalty on any well 'capable of production (whether or not such well has already produced)', which squarely contradicts the prior-production requirement in this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading word is misprinted ('subseauent'), a scanning-level error, but the substance — any well after the initial test well — is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3(B) conditions Subsequent Wells on the test well being completed or plugged, which fits this definition; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite and keyed to the earning mechanics elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with 3(B)(1) and 5(B) (termination as to Unearned Farmout Lands) and with Section 13(B) ('all Farmout Lands have been earned'); the singular/plural drift ('Land' vs 'Lands') is cosmetic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Payout' is defined by gross proceeds equalling drilling, completing and equipping cost, omitting operating costs and saying nothing about whose costs or whether the ORRI is deducted — a genuinely contestable measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Payout is the trigger for the royalty escalations in Section 4.A, whose 'first two (2) wells' and 'all other wells' structure depends on when payout occurs; the definition does not address escalation timing across multiple wells.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The specifications are dated and concrete; 'Farmee's choice' of location is discretionary but expressly so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) says the Agreement terminates 'pursuant to Section[] 3(A)(2)', but 3(A)(2) contains no termination language at all — the termination consequence has to be imported from 3(F), and Section 16 conditions the ROFR on the test well being drilled AND completed by August 31, 1996, whereas 3(A)(2) requires only commencement by that date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'at Farmee's further option, it shall continuously develop' juxtaposes an option with a mandatory 'shall', and 'fully developed' has no defined standard — a named internal contradiction in the drilling commitment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) treats 3(B)(3) as a provision whose breach terminates the Agreement 'as a consequence of Farmee's failure to meet the drilling commitments', which cannot be reconciled with 3(B) making Subsequent Wells optional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'lost for any reason' and a condition rendering drilling 'impractical or impossible' are elastic standards that a party could stretch to excuse abandonment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 3(F)'s time-of-the-essence default rule and with Section 5's plug-and-abandon notice regime, and it is unclear whether a substitute well restarts the 3(A)(2)/3(B)(3) deadlines.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'within sixty (60) days after Farmor is satisfied' makes delivery turn on one party's subjective satisfaction, and the forfeiture in (2) runs from a different event (well completion), so the two sixty-day periods measure from different points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The satisfaction condition incorporates Exhibit C's geologic requirements wholesale and sits against 2(D)'s definition of Operating Rights Earned and Exhibit D's form assignment; the forfeiture-plus-plugging consequence also overlaps Section 5's abandonment procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise depth formula with an express cap; nothing ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 2(F)'s 'Contract Depth' of 4,000' and 2(D)'s areal grant, but Exhibit D reserves everything below a blank '________ formation' rather than below a depth, leaving the two instruments measuring the reservation differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If Farmee defaults, other than above' is an imprecise divider between automatic termination and cure-notice termination, and 'time being of the essence' sits against a thirty-day cure right; the survival of earned Operating Rights is stated three separate ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(A) lists 3(F) as a termination trigger and Section 6 governs the takeover it authorises, yet the automatic-termination limb leaves no room for the 13/5(B) machinery; the plugging obligation that survives termination is also the natural battleground against Section 5.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause contains real mechanical errors — 'Farmor reserved the right to escalate', '5gross proceeds', and 'less than one hundred percent (100%) or the working interest' (evidently 'of the working interest') — and 'reserves the right to escalate' does not say how or when the election is made.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D's form assignment leaves the ORRI percentage blank and adds a severance-tax carve-out that contradicts this section's 'without deductions of any kind', and the survival sentence must be read against Sections 13 and 3(F) on termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'ceases production' is undefined and could mean any interruption or permanent cessation, and 'additional operations as it desires' is unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'ceases production' trigger overlaps awkwardly with the shut-in regime in Section 7(A) and definition 2(H), and Section 3(F) gives Farmor a separate takeover right on default subject to Section 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'without written notification and Farmor's approval' requires approval that Section 5(A) never actually confers — 5(A) gives Farmor only an election to take over, not an approval right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That mismatch with 5(A), plus Section 13(A)'s listing of 5(B) as a termination trigger for the whole Agreement while 5(B) itself terminates only 'as to the Unearned Farmout Lands', is a concrete internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase 'any Operating Rights Earned by Farmor and earned by Farmee' is garbled, and 'estimated salvage value ... less estimated plugging costs' leaves the estimator unidentified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6 by its terms applies only to takeovers 'under ... Section 5', yet 3(F) also invokes a takeover 'subject to the terms of Section 6' for defaulted wells, and the reimbursement duty sits oddly with Farmee's surviving plugging obligation in 3(F).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shut in for any reasontfor a period of Forty Five (45) days or longer' is corrupted text, and an annual $500 royalty 'prorated on a monthly basis' but 'due and payable by the last day of each month' is an unclear payment mechanic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to wells 'whether or not such well has already produced', flatly contradicting the 2(H) definition of 'shut-in well' as one that 'has previously produced'; Exhibit D also makes the assignment continue while the well is 'shut-in pursuant to' this Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wheri possible' is a typo for 'When possible' and is in any event a soft, hard-to-enforce qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the notice regime of 7(A) and Section 10, and no other provision makes shut-in notice mandatory, so it stands alone without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully drafted indemnity; the enumerations are all preceded by 'including but not limited to', so the catch-alls are expressly non-exhaustive, and it is silent on Farmor's own negligence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with Exhibit D's separate indemnity (which runs to operations 'on the premises herein assigned') and with Section 15(C) placing derrick-floor access at Farmor's sole risk; the two indemnities overlap without contradicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line absolute covenant; 'free and clear from all liens' has no exception even for statutory or contested liens.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D expressly gives Assignor 'a lien on all future production and proceeds' for unpaid ORRI, and 15(D) separately bars Farmee from subjecting the Agreement to liens, so the absolute covenant sits against a lien the instrument itself creates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'does not warrant title, either express or implied' is grammatically off (adjectives modifying a verb) but the disclaimer's meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Exhibit D's fuller disclaimer of all warranties; nothing elsewhere promises title.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear delegation to Exhibit C plus a one-year confidentiality period; 'well data and information' is broad but the obligation is symmetrical and time-limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C directs delivery to a different addressee (Attn: Mike Stamper) than the 10(B) notice address (Attn: Lester Zitkus), a minor divergence, and Exhibit C says samples go where 'EREX will have free access' — an entity name never defined in the Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure address block; it lists means of contact but never states when notice is deemed given or whether fax suffices.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit C's delivery address and attention party differ from this one, and 5(A) permits telephone notice in rig-on-location cases, so the 'shall be given as follows' is not exclusive in practice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'acquire and/or maintain' the listed coverages with no stated limits, deductibles or duration beyond 'while operations are being conducted' — the absence of amounts is a real gap but not an ambiguity of a named term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the Section 8 indemnity and the waiver of subrogation in Farmor's favour; no other provision addresses insurance, so no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading 'MODIFICATIONS AND AMENDMENTS' does not match the content, which is an after-acquired-interest clause; 'subsequently acquired interest in such lands' obtained 'directly or indirectly' is broad and undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The instrument contains no amendment or integration clause anywhere, so a reader looking for one is directed by this heading to a provision that supplies none, and the clause extends Section 4.A's reservations beyond the leases described in Exhibit A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall be in effect until such time as' followed by only two exits leaves no ordinary expiry date, and the phrase 'as provided for elsewhere in this Agreement' is a vague cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cites 3(A)(2) and 3(B)(3) as termination provisions although neither contains any termination language, and 3(B)(3) makes Subsequent Wells optional; it also treats 5(B) — which terminates only as to Unearned Farmout Lands — as ending the whole Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two sentences that state the audit right twice with slightly different notice formulations ('upon written notice' then 'thirty (30) days prior'), and no scope limit on records or look-back period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Section 4.A's royalty and Exhibit D's monthly statement obligation; nothing elsewhere restricts or duplicates the audit right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all obligations, burdens and requirements set forth hereunder or otherwise associated with the lands covered hereby' is an unbounded catch-all whose reach beyond the Agreement cannot be fixed from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The undefined external burdens would include the underlying leases, which Section 9 says Farmor does not warrant and Exhibit D makes the assignment 'expressly subject to'; the breadth arguably swallows the specific duties elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'as nearly as possible to its original condition' is an inherently elastic restoration standard, and 'settle surface damages' does not say with whom or on what terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with 5(B)'s cost of 'restoration and reclamation of the surface acreage' and Section 8(A)'s surface-restoration indemnity without contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; 'at all times' and 'authorized representatives' are broad but readily applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'sole risk of Farmor' allocation sits alongside Section 8(A)'s Farmee indemnity for its operations, an ordinary pairing rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat consent requirement across an enumerated list of dispositions; it does not say consent will not be unreasonably withheld, and it is silent on assignments of earned Operating Rights as opposed to the Agreement itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D permits the Assignee to assign well interests on mere written notification down to a 25% working interest, and Section 17 makes the covenants bind 'successors and assigns' and run with the land — a real tension over what Farmee may transfer without consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite reporting obligation with a fixed date and content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside Exhibit D's monthly production statements and Section 14's audit right; duplicative but consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is labelled a 'Right of First Refusal' but operates as a preferential right to a farmout on preset terms with no third-party offer to match; 'during the term of this Agreement' and the fifteen-day deemed-election mechanic add further construction points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its condition precedent — that Farmee 'drills and completes the test well on or before August 31, 1996' — conflicts with Section 3(A), which requires only commencement of drilling by that date and allows completion within forty-five days after total depth.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall run with said Farmout Lands' asserts a real-covenant character without identifying the burdened estates, a contestable characterisation in a short sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Binding 'successors and assigns' and running with the land sits against 15(D)'s absolute bar on assignment without consent, and the effectiveness sentence must be read with the preamble's 'effective as hereinafter provided'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of four deliverables with a fixed number of copies; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'Operator', a term the Agreement never defines but which Section 6 uses in the regulatory sense, a slight mismatch with 'Farmee' used throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains transcription errors ('casinn', 'Cores Shall') and open standards — 'qualified wellsite geologist', 'thoroughly and timely', 'properly and timely analyzed' — that have no measurable boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants free access to 'EREX', an abbreviation nowhere defined in the Agreement (Farmor is 'Equitable Resources Energy Company'), and compliance with Exhibit C is a condition to earning an assignment under 3(D).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Significant indications', 'adequately tested' and 'good oilfield practices' are three stacked vague standards in a single sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because 3(D) conditions the assignment on Farmor being satisfied that all Exhibit C geologic requirements were met, this vague testing duty acquires forfeiture consequences it does not itself acknowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Routine daily prepaid report' is almost certainly a mis-transcription of 'prepared', and a daily report 'Monday through Friday' with daily written confirmation is otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the notice regime of Section 10(A) and the Exhibit C delivery address in D.1; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Non-routine occurrences such as' introduces an illustrative list whose outer limit is undefined, and 'immediately' is unqualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'Farmor's designated representative' where Section 10(B) and Exhibit C D.1 name different individuals, a small internal loose end.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad enumeration ('all reports, charts, logs, analyses, surveys and forms') tied to a definite trigger; little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with C.1 and C.2's copy requirements, though the number of copies specified differs across the exhibit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is a check-box form and the marks are illegible ('i Density', '_ Neutron', blank 'Other'), so which surveys are actually required cannot be determined from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Compliance with Exhibit C is a condition to earning an assignment under 3(D), so an unresolvable checklist has operative consequences elsewhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Timely notice' is undefined and the sufficiency of notice turns on the unstated needs of Farmor's representative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates part of B.3(b)'s immediate-telephone duty for intent to core, test or log without saying how the two interact.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The copy counts contradict themselves within the provision: 'one copy of the following (unless otherwise specified)', then '(a) Two final prints', then a 'THREE COPIES:' header over (b)–(e).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item (e), 'any other data pertinent to the drilling, testing and surveying of the well', is an open catch-all that overlaps B.3(c)'s 'two copies of all reports', producing inconsistent delivery counts across the exhibit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'full information on the completion progress' is an unbounded obligation sitting above a specific list, the classic general-versus-specific tension.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 'completed as a producer' where the Agreement elsewhere turns on completion 'as a well capable of production in paying quantities' (3(D)) and on the 2(A) definition that includes dry holes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'and other similar data' is a mild catch-all, but the delivery instruction is otherwise purely administrative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The addressee (Attn: Mike Stamper, no street suite) differs from the Section 10(B) notice address (Attn: Lester Zitkus), so the two delivery regimes do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A form preamble with the date left blank; nothing ambiguous in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blank date must be supplied to align with the Farmout Agreement dated April 12, 1996, which the exhibit repeatedly leaves undated, but this is form incompleteness rather than contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Every operative particular — well number and the size of the 'acre circle' — is a blank, so the granting language cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blanks are meant to be filled from 2(D) (80-acre gas / 40-acre oil circles), but the form grants 'the right to operate, maintain and rework' where 2(D) says 'operate, maintain and produce', and it references its own Exhibit 'A' distinct from the Agreement's Exhibit A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A habendum in blank; 'produced in paying quantities' is the standard phrase courts construe, and the shut-in limb is left to the Farmout Agreement's terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Section 7(A)'s shut-in royalty and on 2(H)'s definition of a 'shut-in well' requiring prior production, which conflict with each other, so the duration of the assignment inherits that inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A comprehensive disclaimer and indemnity; the enumerated warranty types close with 'or otherwise', and the indemnity covers claims 'incident to, or arising directly or indirectly from' Assignee's operations — broad, but deliberately so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels Section 9's title disclaimer and Section 8(A)'s indemnity, but is narrower (operations 'on the premises herein assigned') than 8(A), leaving the relationship between the two indemnities to be worked out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'necessary or convenient' is a soft boundary on the rights conveyed, and everything is made 'expressly subject to' unidentified underlying deeds and leases.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Section 9's no-warranty stance and Section 15(A)'s duty to comply with obligations associated with the lands; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The royalty rate and the substance produced are both blanks, and the clause creates a lien remedy without stating its priority or enforcement mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves out severance tax ('Assignor shall bear its proportionate part') whereas Section 4.A reserves the ORRI 'without deductions of any kind', and its lien on production sits against 8(B)'s covenant to keep the lands free of all liens.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'grants, conveys and assigns other such rights ... only to the extent set forth herein' is awkwardly worded ('other such rights' has no antecedent), though the reservation of title is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2(D)'s 'that portion and only that portion' limitation and Section 9's title disclaimer; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence requires only notification of an intent to assign while the third requires prior written consent for operator-related assignments, and the 25% working-interest floor assumes a working interest the assignment of operating rights does not expressly convey.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15(D) of the Agreement bars any assignment by Farmee without Farmor's prior written consent, which cannot easily be squared with a notification-only regime for well interests here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reservation is keyed to a blank ('below the ________ formation'), so as written it reserves nothing identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3(E) measures earned depths by feet (100' below total depth, capped at 4,000') rather than by formation, so the assignment form and the Agreement use incompatible yardsticks for the deep rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate successors-and-assigns clause with nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its unqualified reference to 'assigns' sits against 15(D) of the Agreement and the consent restrictions in the preceding Exhibit D paragraph, a familiar boilerplate-versus-restriction tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence subordination to the Farmout Agreement, with the date left blank but the referent unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the assignment subject to an Agreement whose Section 4.A royalty and severance-tax treatment differ from Exhibit D's own royalty paragraph, so the subordination language is what would have to resolve that clash.
